Featured projects
Ac install
Sep 24, 2026

To improve indoor climate control, we installed a new crossover air handler and condenser, ensuring optimal air circulation. We identified supply and return air locations, cut necessary openings, and routed flex ductwork to the trunk line. After securely mounting the condenser, we completed connections for power, refrigerant lines, and installed a thermostat, confirming the system is functioning flawlessly.

Generator installation
Sep 21, 2026

The generator installation has been successfully performed. The generator was positioned on the pad at the designated location, and a new gas line was installed from the gas meter to the generator. The transfer switch was mounted adjacent to the electrical meter, with lines run from the transfer switch to the generator. The gas line was pressure tested and subsequently painted. A simulation of power loss was conducted to test the generator's operation, confirming that the system is functioning properly. The job is now complete.

AC installation
Aug 25, 2026

After completing the installation of the AC unit, the unit was tested, confirming that no additional refrigerant was required and that the system was functioning correctly. A final walkthrough with the homeowner ensured satisfaction with the quality of work performed.

Ac replacement
Aug 20, 2026

The air handler and condenser have been replaced. The refrigerant was recovered, and all old equipment was removed. A fence had to be taken down to transport the condenser to the backyard through the neighbor's property. New equipment was installed, with transitional ductwork utilized to connect the existing ductwork to the new system. The drains and electrical connections were re-established for the air handler. The line set to the air handler was flushed and reconnected, along with the line set and electrical connections to the new condenser. A nitrogen pressure test was performed at 500 psi to check for leaks, and no leaks were identified. A vacuum was pulled below 500 μm before releasing the factory charge of refrigerant. An additional pound of R454B was added to meet the manufacturer's specified subcooling of 8°F. The thermostat was replaced, and the homeowner was provided with operational instructions. The job has been completed.

Furnace/ ac replacement
Aug 6, 2026

The technician successfully completed the removal of the old system located in the utility closet. The installation of the furnace, evaporator coil, and condenser was performed without any issues, ensuring that both heating and cooling functions were operating properly upon job completion. During the appointment, it was noted that the thermostat mentioned in the contract could not be installed due to the requirement of running a new wire, which the customer opted not to pursue. As a result, the old thermostat was reconnected to the system, and the cost associated with the new thermostat was deducted from the remaining balance. A thorough walkthrough was conducted with the customer to ensure satisfaction and understanding of the completed work.

Service
Sep 3, 2026

On arrival customers told me how now the condenser fan doesn’t kick on again so I went ahead and checked the fan itself when I turned the unit on the fan does kick on, but makes an aggressive noise. I went ahead and checked amperage coming from the fan and I was getting 1.8 A.4 more than what the RLA is since that fan was hooked up to its own dual run capacitor. I went ahead and checked that capacitor and saw that it was a bit low at 2.3 µF. Went ahead and unplugged the fan straight into the new capacitor that I had put in yesterday. Turned the system on and it makes significantly less of a noise when turning on. Went ahead and cycled the unit six times to see if the fan continues to come on and the fan continued to come on. Checked amperage from the fan, fan is now reading about 1.1 A. Units and running again.

Hvac service
Aug 28, 2026

On arrival I go ahead and turn power off to the air handler and begin disassembling the old motor out of the housing and wheel shaft was a bit corroded so it made it a bit difficult to pull out the motor after pulling out the motor installed the new one made sure the wheel sat correctly and tight on the motor shaft put the housing and motor back into place wired up the motor exactly how the old one was closed up the unit and started it up. Fan kicked on immediately. AC is up and running again.

Hvac & Generator maintenance
Aug 27, 2026

Arrived at the location to perform a generator maintenance, turned on the generator, changed oil, oil filter, air filter and spark plugs. Checked battery, wire and wires connections. Simulated power outage make sure the generator turned on and transferred power back to the home. Run hours 19, calibrate 1=1504, calibrate 2=1531, battery 13. Mini split two zone I perform a mini splits maintenance, check t/stat and start system operation, clean condenser unit, check refrigerant pressures, check amps draws, clean and wash air filter , clean and flush condensation drains and traps , check blowers motors , check t/d , check all wires and connections. Master bedroom I replaced the mini-split louver and louver motor, then verified that it was working properly.

Furnace/ ac replacement
Aug 6, 2026

The technician successfully completed the removal of the old system located in the utility closet. The installation of the furnace, evaporator coil, and condenser was performed without any issues, ensuring that both heating and cooling functions were operating properly upon job completion. During the appointment, it was noted that the thermostat mentioned in the contract could not be installed due to the requirement of running a new wire, which the customer opted not to pursue. As a result, the old thermostat was reconnected to the system, and the cost associated with the new thermostat was deducted from the remaining balance. A thorough walkthrough was conducted with the customer to ensure satisfaction and understanding of the completed work.

Nov 2, 2026

A malfunctioning hot water boiler was impacting the comfort of the home. We performed comprehensive maintenance under a silver agreement, ensuring optimal operation and safety. Our skilled technicians meticulously checked all components, performed necessary adjustments, and verified the system's efficiency to provide reliable hot water service for the household.

Nov 2, 2026

A malfunction in the heating system was affecting the comfort of the space. We addressed the issue by servicing System 2 on the right side, which included the furnace, thermostat, return plenum, supply plenum, and surge protector. This comprehensive work ensured optimal performance and reliability, enhancing the overall functionality of the heating system.

Oct 29, 2026

An issue arose with the HVAC system during maintenance due to access constraints in the washer and dryer room. We efficiently navigated the tight space, utilizing a small extension ladder to reach the attic. Our team conducted a thorough inspection and performed necessary maintenance, ensuring optimal airflow and system performance while applying an environmental fee for responsible waste disposal.

About Bloomfield Cooling, Heating & Electric

Our goal at Bloomfield Cooling, Heating & Electric, Inc. is simple: to consistently provide high-quality heating and air conditioning equipment, installations, service, and repair to our residential and commercial customers in Bergen, Passaic, Hudson, Morris, Union and Essex counties.

Superior heating and cooling products backed by excellent service

We use only the best HVAC products and generators on the market and are proud to sell and support Carrier products. Our customer service support staff and equipment installers and technicians are all committed to delivering superior service.

We always go the extra mile to determine our clients’ optimal needs and provide knowledgeable advice, skilled craftsmanship, and an unparalleled dedication to performance. It all starts with your initial phone call to our office and our helpful support staff. From there, our highly skilled comfort consultant will come to your premises for a full system evaluation, answer all your questions, and create a custom heating/cooling solution, including custom HVAC projects for unusual spaces. Our certified technicians and equipment installers will get the job done with the utmost professionalism. Our team treats your premises just as we do our own, with care and attention to detail.

As professionals committed to quality in every aspect of our business, we practice the highest level of ethics with our customers and treat our employees and suppliers with respect, dignity, and fairness.

Our history: growth, expansion, employee development

Bloomfield Cooling, Heating & Cooling, Inc. was established in 1989 by Michael DeJoseph in Bloomfield, NJ as a heating and cooling company, moving to a one-room office Nutley in 1991, where we quickly began to grow. We moved to a larger location and in 1993, we added an electrical division to provide more efficient service to our customers.

With a reputation for fast, reliable service, professionalism, and immaculate installations we continued to grow and in 2005 Bloomfield Cooling, Heating & Electric moved to Little Falls, where we have our central office, a large warehouse, conference room, sheet metal shop, and our fleet of vans. We added installation and service of home standby generators in 2006 and in 2020 added various in-duct and whole-home air purifiers to our product line.

In January 2025 our general manager, Jack Lamb, who joined Bloomfield Cooling, Heating & Electric in 2000, became the new owner when our founder and president, Michael DeJoseph, retired.

Jack began his career with us as a full-time electrician and over time, Jack learned HVAC service work and system installations, ran the service department, and became general manager in 2014. He said he owes his professional evolution and expanded knowledge of the HVAC industry to Mike DeJoseph—and now he oversees the professional development of our team members while also enhancing our customer service capabilities.
